title: Series or parallel: why one dead bulb matters
examples: What is the difference between series and parallel circuits?
Why do all the lights go out when one bulb breaks?
Why are houses wired in parallel?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Homes are wired in parallel so each device works alone.

explain.say: There are two ways to join several bulbs to one battery: in series, one after another, or in parallel, each on its own branch.

draw.verdict: Homes are wired in parallel so each device works alone.

explain.say: In series there is one single loop, so the bulbs share the battery's voltage and glow dimmer, and if one breaks, the loop is broken and they all go out.

draw.verdict: Homes are wired in parallel so each device works alone.

explain.say: In parallel each bulb has its own branch straight to the battery, so each gets the full voltage and glows brightly.

explain.say: And if one bulb in parallel breaks, only its branch stops; current still flows through the others. That is why homes are wired in parallel.

nodes.label: Broken bulb
nodes.ask: What happens if one bulb breaks in a parallel circuit?

faq.a: In a series circuit the parts are joined one after another in a single loop. The same current flows through every part, and they share the battery's voltage.
asks: Why do all the lights go out in series?

faq.a: In a parallel circuit each part sits on its own branch across the battery. Each branch gets the full voltage, and the branch currents add up to the total.
asks: Why are houses wired in parallel?

faq.q: What happens if one bulb breaks in a parallel circuit?
faq.a: Only that branch stops. The other branches still make complete loops with the battery, so their bulbs stay lit.
asks: Do the other bulbs stay on in parallel?

faq.q: Why are bulbs dimmer in series?
faq.a: Two identical bulbs in series share the voltage, so each gets half. With less push, less current flows and each glows more dimly than a bulb on its own.
asks: Why does adding bulbs in series make them dimmer?

faq.q: Does a parallel circuit drain the battery faster?
faq.a: Yes. Each branch draws its own current, so the total current is bigger and the battery runs down faster, even though every bulb is bright.
asks: Which circuit makes a battery last longer?

facts: In a series circuit the current is the same everywhere; in a parallel circuit each branch has the same voltage.
Old-style fairy lights wired in series would all go out when one bulb failed.

quiz.say: Two bulbs are wired in parallel and one breaks. What happens to the other?
quiz.show: Two bulbs are wired in parallel and one breaks. What happens to the other?
quiz.why: The other bulb is on its own branch, which is still a complete loop with the battery.

wrong.1: That happens in series, where there is only one loop.
wrong.2: Its branch still gets the full battery voltage, so its brightness hardly changes.
